newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gingrich taps views of a divided Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich taps views of a divided Hong Kong.

text.p: U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich said on Wednesday the eyes of the world would monitor how China handles the takeover of Hong Kong later this year.

Gingrich arrived from South Korea for a two-day visit en route to China and spent the day tapping the views of a wide spectrum of Hong Kong opinion, ranging from wary human rights activists to confident members of Hong Kong's pro-Beijing business community.

On Thursday he will meet Governor Chris Patten, who introduced greater democracy into Hong Kong to China's fury and his designated successor, businessman Tung Chee-hwa who supports China's plans to undo many of Patten's reforms.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to China at midnight on June 30, now just 97 days away.

Opinion polls show the 6.4 million inhabitants of the wealthy territory to be relatively confident about Hong Kong's economic future under China but concerned about Beijing's plans to roll back democratic reforms and civil liberties.

"We agreed that the maximum implementation of the rule of law, of the legitimate authority of an elected legislative body and of a relationship which are truly two systems, one country is vital," Gingrich told reporters when he emerged from a roundtable discussion with Hong Kong legislators.
The 1984 Sino-British treaty governing the handover committed China to maintaining Hong Kong's capitalist way of life, under late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's "one country, two systems" formula.
